raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Base and scope

Retargeted to `main` after the model integration landed in #37500 (replacing #36497). Rebased onto `01f684069351` on October 13; current head `99755df6008d` includes the required `60878c3fba50` CI baseline. The main-branch resolver still accepts an importable FA4 fallback on SM89 when classic FA2 is missing; this PR keeps its SM89 preflight fix independent of the model-support stack.

## Motivation

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next currently fails late on NVIDIA L20 / SM89 when the image does not contain classic FlashAttention / FA2:

```text
FlashInfer TRTLLM resolver -> unavailable on SM89
classic flash_attn / FA2    -> not importable
flash_attn.cute / FA4       -> importable, so the resolver selects it
first sparse decode         -> CuTe MLIR operation creation failure
```

On four L20s with the released FP8 checkpoint, the server loaded the approximately 173 GB checkpoint and became HTTP-ready before the first generation request failed in the FA4/CuTe path. Importability is therefore not a sufficient compatibility check, and the failure happens after the most expensive part of startup.

## Modifications

- Represent the resolved QSA sparse-decode backend explicitly as `TRTLLM`, `TRITON_ROCM`, `KDA_SM121`, classic `FA2`, or `FA4_CUTE` and use the same result for preflight and runtime dispatch.
- Reject the FA4/CuTe fallback only on exact SM89 when classic FA2 is unavailable, with an actionable error.
- Run the QSA check before `ModelRunner.load_model()` and log the selected backend once on TP rank zero.
- Keep the QSA implementation lazily imported for non-QSA models.
- Preserve the existing TRTLLM route on SM100/SM120, dedicated KDA route on SM121, and import-based policy on SM90. Preserve the current ROCm Triton packed-decode path without requiring FA2/FA4/aiter, and retain the existing aiter varlen helper. The behavioral change is intentionally limited to the hardware reproduced here.

## Independence / related work

- #36806 changes the exact SM120 FlashInfer route; it does not add an SM89 path or preflight.
- Draft #36787 adds SM120 kernels and leaves the existing flash-attn fallback on other architectures, including SM89.
- #36531 and #36558 track SM12x failures, not L20 / SM89.

The October 13 main snapshot still permits the import-based FA4 fallback on SM89. A targeted October 13 search of PR titles/bodies for QSA and SM89 found this PR and the separate L20 MoE-config PR, but no equivalent preflight implementation. This does not exclude other ongoing or unindexed work.

## Tests

### October 13: current head `99755df6008d`, real NVIDIA L20 / SM89

Fresh Python 3.12 environment with dependencies resolved from this head's `python/pyproject.toml`, without inheriting the old image's Python packages. Core versions: torch `2.14.1+cu130`, FlashInfer `0.7.1`, flash-attn-4 `4.0.0b34`, Triton `3.8.0`, transformers `5.19.0`, sglang-kernel `0.4.9`. Imported source files match this head. No dependency-version checks were disabled.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Registered policy tests + upstream ROCm resolver cases | **19 passed, 2 subtests passed** in each of three runs; one actual ROCm kernel test deselected on NVIDIA |
| Real SM89 preflight, FA2 absent / FA4 importable | Expected actionable error; 0 MiB allocated tensor memory |
| Full `launch_server`, FA2 absent | **Two consistent expected failures: 50.08 s and 49.16 s**, before weight loading |
| Real SM89 preflight after installing classic FA2 | Selects and logs `classic FlashAttention / FA2` |
| Selected FA2 kernel vs FP32 reference | **16/16 passed**: FP16/BF16, two seeds, four KV-length patterns |
| Installed dependency consistency | `uv pip check`: all 211 installed packages compatible |

The full-startup tests use the real local Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 checkpoint configuration, TP1, and disabled CUDA graphs. Both stack traces reach `ModelRunner.initialize -> preflight_model_backends -> preflight_qsa_sparse_decode_backend` and raise:

```text
RuntimeError: QSA sparse decode on NVIDIA SM89 requires classic FlashAttention / FA2,
but it is not importable. FlashAttention-4 / CuTe is not a validated QSA fallback
on SM89/Ada. Install a compatible FA2 build before starting SGLang.
```

Neither log contains `Load weight begin`; the model-runner memory baseline is 0.00 GB. An earlier attempt in the old image stopped at its FlashInfer version gate and is not counted as a passing startup test.

FA2 parity mirrors the QSA varlen call: 24 Q heads, 2 KV heads, head dimension 256, one query per row, `causal=True`, and KV lengths `[1]`, `[64]`, `[0,1,17]`, `[31,0,129,257]`. Maximum absolute error against the FP32 reference was **5.49e-4 for FP16** and **4.17e-3 for BF16**. Empty rows and extra packed-buffer capacity are included. Tolerances: FP16 `atol=0.002, rtol=0.005`; BF16 `atol=0.01, rtol=0.01`.

Build disclosure: classic FA2 `2.8.3.post1` was compiled locally with only its two CUDA/C++ build-standard flags changed to C++20, following upstream [#2879](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/pull/2879) / [#2899](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/pull/2899) for newer Torch headers. FA2 kernel sources were unchanged; this experiment-only build adaptation is not part of this SGLang PR.

### Check that newer FA4 has not already removed the failure

FA4 `4.0.0b34` does contain an SM8x forward path, so this is **not a claim that FA4 is universally unsupported on Ada**. Directly exercising the same varlen interface on L20 with the actual QSA head dimension 256 still fails all eight FP16/BF16 × KV-length cases with CUDA launch/configuration errors. Changing only the head dimension to 128 passes all eight numerical-control cases.

Minimal reproduction of the failing QSA shape, in that environment:

```python
import torch
from flash_attn.cute.interface import flash_attn_varlen_func

q = torch.randn(1, 24, 256, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
k = torch.randn(71, 2, 256, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
v = torch.randn_like(k)
cu_q = torch.tensor([0, 1], device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
cu_k = torch.tensor([0, 64], device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
flash_attn_varlen_func(q=q, k=k, v=v, cu_seqlens_q=cu_q,
                      cu_seqlens_k=cu_k, max_seqlen_q=1, max_seqlen_k=64,
                      softmax_scale=256**-0.5, causal=True)
```

The registered suite covers SM89, SM90, SM100, SM120, SM121, ROCm's no-varlen-dependency path, non-QSA lazy no-op, rank-zero logging, and exception propagation. Other architectures are policy/unit coverage, not hardware validation. Ruff, isort, registered-test taxonomy, and whitespace checks passed.

The [independent RTX 4090 report](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36968#issuecomment-6142214847) supports the original failure and workaround; it is not counted as testing this head. These results validate fail-fast and the selected kernel, **not successful full-model 176B serving, CUDA-graph capture, throughput, or complete upstream CI**.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. This changes startup validation and backend observability, not a kernel or successful inference path.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code according to the contribution guide.
- [x] Add registered regression tests.
- [x] Validate the original failure boundary on real SM89 hardware.
- [x] Preserve non-SM89 behavior.
- [x] No documentation update is needed because no user-facing flag or API is added.

nodes.body:
Validated this fix direction on real hardware: 8x RTX 4090 (sm89), `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8`, tp4/ep4, 262K context, PLE offload enabled.

Preinstalling classic FA2 `2.8.3.post1` (built from sdist against `torch==2.13.0+cu130`, `FLASH_ATTN_CUDA_ARCHS=80;90;100;120`) makes the exact crash described here disappear: the QSA resolver picks classic FA2, server serves fine, throughput on par with vLLM on the same hardware and checkpoint.

One extra data point for anyone shipping classic FA2 in a shared image: with classic FA2 importable, `_resolve_flash_attn_varlen_func()` also selects it on sm120 (RTX 5090 / RTX PRO 6000), so build the 100/120 archs too (the upstream default arch set already does) or Blackwell machines get an importable-but-kernelless FA2. The sm121/GB10 branch is unaffected.

Without the fail-fast here, users burn a 10-20 minute full weights load before hitting the CuTe error, which is very far from the real cause. Would love to see this merged.

Thanks @aisensiy for the hardware validation and packaging notes! I've updated the PR with L20 fail-fast and FA2 correctness results; details are in the description. Lint passed. Could a maintainer enable `run-ci` and review when convenient? Thanks!

+"""Early validation for QSA runtime backend dependencies."""
+
+import logging
+
+from sglang.srt.layers.attention.qsa.config import is_qwen_qsa
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+
+def _resolve_qsa_sparse_decode_backend():
+    # Keep the large QSA implementation lazy for every non-QSA model.
+    from sglang.srt.layers.attention.qwen_sparse_attn_backend import (
+        resolve_qsa_sparse_decode_backend,
+    )
+
+    return resolve_qsa_sparse_decode_backend()
+
+
+def preflight_qsa_sparse_decode_backend(*, model_config, tp_rank: int) -> None:
+    """Validate and report QSA sparse decode before model weight loading."""
+
+    if not is_qwen_qsa(model_config.hf_text_config):
+        return
+    backend = _resolve_qsa_sparse_decode_backend()
+    if tp_rank == 0:
+        logger.info("QSA sparse decode backend: %s", backend.kind.value)
+
+
+__all__ = ["preflight_qsa_sparse_decode_backend"]

+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+from sglang.srt.layers.attention import qwen_sparse_attn_backend as qsa
+from sglang.srt.layers.attention.qsa import preflight as qsa_preflight
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+class TestQSASparseDecodeBackendResolution(CustomTestCase):
+    """Regress late FA4 selection on unsupported NVIDIA architectures.
+
+    On SM89, an importable FA4 was previously selected when classic FA2 was
+    absent and failed only after model loading. The matrix also verifies that
+    the existing SM90/SM100/SM120/SM121 policies remain unchanged.
+    """
+
+    def setUp(self):
+        super().setUp()
+        qsa._resolve_sm121_kda_sparse_decode.cache_clear()
+        qsa.resolve_qsa_sparse_decode_backend.cache_clear()
+
+    def tearDown(self):
+        qsa._resolve_sm121_kda_sparse_decode.cache_clear()
+        qsa.resolve_qsa_sparse_decode_backend.cache_clear()
+        super().tearDown()
+
+    def _resolve(self, capability, *, trtllm=None, sm121_kda=None, fa2=None, fa4=None):
+        with (
+            patch.object(qsa, "is_hip", return_value=False),
+            patch.object(qsa.torch.version, "hip", None),
+            patch.object(qsa, "_nvidia_compute_capability", return_value=capability),
+            patch.object(qsa, "_resolve_trtllm_sparse_decode", return_value=trtllm),
+            patch.object(
+                qsa,
+                "_resolve_sm121_kda_sparse_decode",
+                return_value=sm121_kda,
+            ) as resolve_sm121_kda,
+            patch.object(
+                qsa, "_resolve_classic_fa2_sparse_decode", return_value=fa2
+            ) as resolve_fa2,
+            patch.object(
+                qsa, "_resolve_fa4_cute_sparse_decode", return_value=fa4
+            ) as resolve_fa4,
+        ):
+            result = qsa.resolve_qsa_sparse_decode_backend()
+        return result, resolve_sm121_kda, resolve_fa2, resolve_fa4
+
+    def test_sm89_uses_classic_fa2(self):
+        fa2 = object()
+        result, _, _, resolve_fa4 = self._resolve((8, 9), fa2=fa2, fa4=object())
+        self.assertEqual(result.kind, qsa.QSASparseDecodeBackendKind.FA2)
+        self.assertIs(result.kernel, fa2)
+        resolve_fa4.assert_not_called()
+
+    def test_rocm_packed_decode_does_not_require_varlen_dependencies(self):
+        with (
+            patch.object(qsa, "is_hip", return_value=True),
+            patch.object(qsa, "_resolve_trtllm_sparse_decode") as trtllm,
+            patch.object(qsa, "_resolve_sm121_kda_sparse_decode") as kda,
+            patch.object(qsa, "_resolve_classic_fa2_sparse_decode") as fa2,
+            patch.object(qsa, "_resolve_fa4_cute_sparse_decode") as fa4,
+        ):
+            result = qsa.resolve_qsa_sparse_decode_backend()
+        self.assertEqual(result.kind, qsa.QSASparseDecodeBackendKind.TRITON_ROCM)
+        self.assertIs(result.kernel, qsa.sparse_gqa_packed_decode_triton)
+        for resolver in (trtllm, kda, fa2, fa4):
+            resolver.assert_not_called()
+
+    def test_sm120_preserves_classic_fa2_when_trtllm_is_missing(self):
+        fa2 = object()
+        result, _, _, resolve_fa4 = self._resolve((12, 0), fa2=fa2, fa4=object())
+        self.assertEqual(result.kind, qsa.QSASparseDecodeBackendKind.FA2)
+        self.assertIs(result.kernel, fa2)
+        resolve_fa4.assert_not_called()
+
+    def test_sm89_does_not_fall_back_to_fa4_when_fa2_is_missing(self):
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "SM89 requires classic"):
+            self._resolve((8, 9), fa4=object())
+
+    def test_sm89_reports_missing_fa2_when_both_imports_are_absent(self):
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "SM89 requires classic"):
+            self._resolve((8, 9))
+
+    def test_other_architectures_report_missing_fallback_dependencies(self):
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ImportError, "QSA decode requires"):
+            self._resolve((9, 0))
+
+    def test_sm90_uses_classic_fa2(self):
+        fa2 = object()
+        result, _, _, resolve_fa4 = self._resolve((9, 0), fa2=fa2, fa4=object())
+        self.assertEqual(result.kind, qsa.QSASparseDecodeBackendKind.FA2)
+        self.assertIs(result.kernel, fa2)
+        resolve_fa4.assert_not_called()
+
+    def test_sm90_preserves_fa4_fallback_when_fa2_is_missing(self):
+        fa4 = object()
+        result, _, _, _ = self._resolve((9, 0), fa4=fa4)
+        self.assertEqual(result.kind, qsa.QSASparseDecodeBackendKind.FA4_CUTE)
+        self.assertIs(result.kernel, fa4)
+
+    def test_sm100_prefers_trtllm(self):
+        trtllm = object()
+        result, resolve_sm121_kda, resolve_fa2, resolve_fa4 = self._resolve(
+            (10, 0), trtllm=trtllm, fa2=object(), fa4=object()
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(result.kind, qsa.QSASparseDecodeBackendKind.TRTLLM)
+        self.assertIs(result.kernel, trtllm)
+        resolve_sm121_kda.assert_not_called()
+        resolve_fa2.assert_not_called()
+        resolve_fa4.assert_not_called()
+
+    def test_sm100_uses_fa4_when_trtllm_is_missing(self):
+        fa4 = object()
+        result, _, _, _ = self._resolve((10, 0), fa4=fa4)
+        self.assertEqual(result.kind, qsa.QSASparseDecodeBackendKind.FA4_CUTE)
+        self.assertIs(result.kernel, fa4)
+
+    def test_sm120_uses_trtllm(self):
+        trtllm = object()
+        result, resolve_sm121_kda, resolve_fa2, resolve_fa4 = self._resolve(
+            (12, 0), trtllm=trtllm, fa2=object(), fa4=object()
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(result.kind, qsa.QSASparseDecodeBackendKind.TRTLLM)
+        self.assertIs(result.kernel, trtllm)
+        resolve_sm121_kda.assert_not_called()
+        resolve_fa2.assert_not_called()
+        resolve_fa4.assert_not_called()
+
+    def test_sm121_preserves_existing_kda_backend(self):
+        sm121_kda = object()
+        result, _, resolve_fa2, resolve_fa4 = self._resolve(
+            (12, 1), sm121_kda=sm121_kda, fa2=object(), fa4=object()
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(result.kind, qsa.QSASparseDecodeBackendKind.KDA_SM121)
+        self.assertIs(result.kernel, sm121_kda)
+        resolve_fa2.assert_not_called()
+        resolve_fa4.assert_not_called()
+
+
+class TestQSASparseDecodePreflight(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_non_qsa_model_does_not_resolve_qsa_backend(self):
+        model_config = SimpleNamespace(hf_text_config=object())
+        with (
+            patch.object(qsa_preflight, "is_qwen_qsa", return_value=False),
+            patch.object(
+                qsa_preflight, "_resolve_qsa_sparse_decode_backend"
+            ) as resolve,
+        ):
+            qsa_preflight.preflight_qsa_sparse_decode_backend(
+                model_config=model_config, tp_rank=0
+            )
+        resolve.assert_not_called()
+
+    def test_qsa_model_logs_selected_backend_on_rank_zero(self):
+        model_config = SimpleNamespace(hf_text_config=object())
+        backend = SimpleNamespace(kind=SimpleNamespace(value="classic FA2"))
+        with (
+            patch.object(qsa_preflight, "is_qwen_qsa", return_value=True),
+            patch.object(
+                qsa_preflight,
+                "_resolve_qsa_sparse_decode_backend",
+                return_value=backend,
+            ),
+            patch.object(qsa_preflight.logger, "info") as log_info,
+        ):
+            qsa_preflight.preflight_qsa_sparse_decode_backend(
+                model_config=model_config, tp_rank=0
+            )
+        log_info.assert_called_once_with("QSA sparse decode backend: %s", "classic FA2")
+
+    def test_qsa_worker_rank_checks_backend_without_logging(self):
+        model_config = SimpleNamespace(hf_text_config=object())
+        with (
+            patch.object(qsa_preflight, "is_qwen_qsa", return_value=True),
+            patch.object(
+                qsa_preflight, "_resolve_qsa_sparse_decode_backend"
+            ) as resolve,
+            patch.object(qsa_preflight.logger, "info") as log_info,
+        ):
+            qsa_preflight.preflight_qsa_sparse_decode_backend(
+                model_config=model_config, tp_rank=1
+            )
+        resolve.assert_called_once_with()
+        log_info.assert_not_called()
+
+    def test_qsa_preflight_propagates_missing_backend_on_every_rank(self):
+        model_config = SimpleNamespace(hf_text_config=object())
+        for rank in (0, 1):
+            with (
+                self.subTest(tp_rank=rank),
+                patch.object(qsa_preflight, "is_qwen_qsa", return_value=True),
+                patch.object(
+                    qsa_preflight,
+                    "_resolve_qsa_sparse_decode_backend",
+                    side_effect=RuntimeError("SM89 requires classic FA2"),
+                ),
+                self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "SM89 requires classic"),
+            ):
+                qsa_preflight.preflight_qsa_sparse_decode_backend(
+                    model_config=model_config, tp_rank=rank
+                )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

issue_comments.body:
Validated this fix direction on real hardware: 8x RTX 4090 (sm89), `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8`, tp4/ep4, 262K context, PLE offload enabled.

Preinstalling classic FA2 `2.8.3.post1` (built from sdist against `torch==2.13.0+cu130`, `FLASH_ATTN_CUDA_ARCHS=80;90;100;120`) makes the exact crash described here disappear: the QSA resolver picks classic FA2, server serves fine, throughput on par with vLLM on the same hardware and checkpoint.

One extra data point for anyone shipping classic FA2 in a shared image: with classic FA2 importable, `_resolve_flash_attn_varlen_func()` also selects it on sm120 (RTX 5090 / RTX PRO 6000), so build the 100/120 archs too (the upstream default arch set already does) or Blackwell machines get an importable-but-kernelless FA2. The sm121/GB10 branch is unaffected.

Without the fail-fast here, users burn a 10-20 minute full weights load before hitting the CuTe error, which is very far from the real cause. Would love to see this merged.

Thanks @aisensiy for the hardware validation and packaging notes! I've updated the PR with L20 fail-fast and FA2 correctness results; details are in the description. Lint passed. Could a maintainer enable `run-ci` and review when convenient? Thanks!
